summary: Join our comprehensive training on credit risk management tailored for central banks. Equip yourself with essential tools to navigate financial uncertainties.
lede: Credit risk management for central banks provides a structured way to identify, measure, limit, monitor, and report issuer and counterparty risk across reserve portfolios, monetary policy operations, collateralized lending, derivatives, deposits, settlement arrangements, and banking relationships. The course connects PD-LGD-EAD analysis, concentration limits, collateral haircuts, early-warning indicators, and emerging-loss reporting to decisions that can be explained to risk committees, auditors, policy leaders, and operational teams. You will practise building an internal rating scorecard, calculating expected credit loss in Microsoft Excel, mapping settlement dependencies, drafting counterparty limit proposals, creating collateral eligibility matrices, designing stress scenarios, and configuring a Microsoft Power BI dashboard. Workshops address exposure assessment, collateral risk, limit monitoring, governance decisions, and AI-assisted surveillance while recognising practical constraints such as limited default data, inconsistent ratings, legacy systems, restricted liquidity, and the need for data lineage, model validation, human review, and clear escalation ownership.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess, control, monitor, audit, or report credit risk management exposures arising from central bank financial operations.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working knowledge of credit, treasury, reserve management, monetary operations, banking, or financial risk is expected. Basic Microsoft Excel proficiency is recommended. Technology: Bring a laptop with Excel installed. Power BI Desktop supports the dashboard lab where installation policies permit it. Instructor-provided datasets and templates support all practical exercises. Technical depth: Credit measurement, collateral, counterparty assessment, and reporting receive operational application. AI-assisted analysis and emergency liquidity considerations receive conceptual awareness. Coding or programming is not required.
